newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Monday were inactive, with no reported sales, feedlot sources said.
Light packer bids at $65.00 per cwt were passed by owners seeking $67.00 to $68.00 for their cattle, they said.
Sales were not expected to take place until midweek following last week's heavy sales volume, the bulk of which occured at $66.00, sources said.
Prices this week were seen steady, possibly $1.00 higher at $66.00-$67.00, supported by ideas packer demand would remain strong this week.

Feedlot cattle prices also could be underpinned by talk that a lot of cattle on showlists were underfinished because of very current marketings this winter, said Dave Maher, anlalyst with Securities Corp of Iowa.

However, gains could be offset if some feedlots in Nebraska were willing to unload cattle at lower prices to get them off feedlots before warmer temperatures melt snow and turn lots muddy this week, Maher said.
Mud was not seen as a problem in Kansas and the Panhandle area because of less snow there. Also, wind over the weekend helped dry some lots, several cattle feeders said.
